euronews.description: Assisted suicide is legal in several countries, including Belgium, Canada, the Netherlands, Spain and Switzerland, as well as parts of the US, although eligibility rules vary.

euronews.description: Experts and diplomats tell Euronews that Europe’s failure to appropriately respond to escalating Russia aggression across NATO territory is chipping away at the alliance’s deterrence ability – and feeding the Kremlin’s appetite for risk.

euronews.description: Article 123 of the EU treaty prohibits the ECB from cancelling government debt that it has purchased.

euronews.description: Norway’s King has announced that the flag will be flown at half-mast from the Palace balcony on Friday and on the day of her funeral.

euronews.description: More than 552 GW of utility-scale solar and wind projects have been announced, or are already under development, across the Mediterranean.

euronews.title: Are you smarter than a 15-year-old? Test your maths, science and reading with these PISA questions
euronews.description: This week, the OECD's PISA report has revealed a global decline in 15-year-old's maths and reading skills — but how much better can the grown-up's fare?

euronews.title: Colombia’s Cali remembers earthquake victims one month on
euronews.description: Residents of Cali gathered to honour those killed in the August 10 earthquake, releasing white balloons and laying flowers one month after the disaster.

euronews.title: Russian assets are not the focus now, Brussels says as calls for action grow louder
euronews.description: The European Commission is not willing to reopen the contentious debate on the immbolised Russian assets, at least not without a guarantee of success. "Now, the focus is somewhere else," the executive insists.

euronews.title: French ESA astronaut Thomas Pesquet: Europe must 'maximise scientific return' from ISS before closure
euronews.description: The French astronaut urged Europe and his home country to "maximise the scientific return" from the European Space Agency's next mission to the International Space Station, while stressing the importance of spaceflight for Europe’s strategic sovereignty in space.

euronews.title: Houthis seize key Yemeni island in Bab el-Mandeb, taking control of the strait
euronews.description: Houthi fighters reached Perim Island which divides the Bab el-Mandeb into two shipping lanes after government forces withdrew, completing the group's takeover of the strait. Together with Iran's Hormuz blockade, this puts roughly a third of the world's seaborne trade under hostile control.

euronews.title: France cuts growth forecast as economy lags behind European neighbours
euronews.description: It comes after France's national statistics office lowered its forecast for 2026 growth from 0.7% to 0.4% and warned that the French economy was "losing ground."

euronews.title: EU pledges €6.1bn for Ukraine, including aid for Patriot interceptors
euronews.description: Brussels is trying to persuade EU countries that still have Patriot interceptors in their national stockpiles to donate them to Ukraine and replace them at a later stage with deliveries scheduled for 2027.

euronews.title: EU needs to 'pin down' Ukraine's exact budget needs, Dombrovskis tells Euronews
euronews.description: In an interview with Euronews, Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis says the "open questions" surrounding Ukraine's budget needs must first be clarified. Kyiv has asked its allies to plug a €23 billion funding shortfall.

rfi.title: How 100 days of record ocean heat is reshaping life in and around the seas
rfi.description: Global oceans have endured 100 consecutive days of record average heat, as human-driven climate change pushes temperatures higher and puts growing pressure on marine life. Scientists say prolonged warming is disrupting fisheries, damaging coral reefs, raising sea levels and threatening economies that depend on healthy seas.

rfi.title: France cuts growth forecast again as economic uncertainty weighs heavy
rfi.description: France's economy will grow less than expected in 2026, meaning the government will miss its budget deficit target, Finance Minister Roland Lescure has said. It is the third time this year the government has cut its growth forecast.

rfi.title: French 9/11 prisoner seeks to serve life sentence back in France
rfi.description: Zacarias Moussaoui, a French national and the only person convicted in the United States over the 11 September attacks, has asked to serve the rest of his life sentence in France, his lawyer has said.

rfi.title: On 25th anniversary of 9/11, New York remembers victims poisoned by debris
rfi.description: On the 25th anniversary of the 11 September attacks on the World Trade Center, the official 9/11 ceremony in New York will for the first time include a moment of silence dedicated to the thousands who have since died from illnesses linked to their exposure to pollution released when the Twin Towers fell.

rfi.title: Hunt starts to replace chief organiser of France's 2030 Winter Olympics
rfi.description: The search is underway for a new chief of the organising committee for the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps after Edgar Grospiron resigned.

rfi.title: Children killed in stampede as fire sweeps through schools in eastern DRC
rfi.description: At least 27 schoolchildren were killed in a stampede as they tried to escape a fire that swept through two schools in the rebel-held city of Bukavu in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo on Thursday, local authorities said.

rfi.title: Putin in India for Brics summit overshadowed by war
rfi.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin was in India on Friday for talks ahead of an 11-member Brics summit dominated by conflict and economic challenges, with the leaders of China and Iran set to attend.

rfi.title: Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics ‘a bridge to 2028 Los Angeles Games’
rfi.description: Senegal is preparing to make Olympic history when Dakar hosts the Youth Olympic Games from 31 October to 13 November – the first Olympic event ever staged in Africa. But beyond the 13 days of competition, the bigger test will be what the Games leave behind for Senegalese sport.

rfi.title: Algeria cuts diplomatic ties with UAE after years of mounting tensions
rfi.description: Algeria cut diplomatic ties with the United Arab Emirates on Thursday after years of tension, accusing Abu Dhabi of interfering in national and regional affairs.

rfi.title: Macron calls for European crewed spaceflights within 10 years
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday called for Europe to become one of the world’s leading space powers, with its first crewed flights within 10 years and its own satellite-based communications capabilities.

rfi.title: French football chiefs withdraw backing for Fifa boss Infantino
rfi.description: The French Football Federation (FFF) withdrew its support for Gianni Infantino's bid for a fourth term as Fifa president on Thursday, criticising his plans to bring private investors into Fifa's commercial operations and the way he runs the 122-year-old organisation.

rfi.title: French police officers suspended over racist video as far-right links emerge
rfi.description: Four municipal police officers in the southern French city of Carcassonne remain suspended on Thursday as prosecutors investigate racist, sexist and homophobic remarks caught on a police body camera.

rfi.title: New Caledonia activists file complaint against French ministers over 2024 riots
rfi.description: Six Kanak pro-independence activists have filed a complaint against four current or former French ministers, accusing them of orchestrating their arrests and transfers from New Caledonia to prisons in mainland France for political reasons during the Pacific territory's 2024 unrest.

rfi.title: Bayeux Tapestry 'mania' sweeps UK as sold-out exhibition opens
rfi.description: London's sold-out Bayeux Tapestry exhibition opens on Thursday to a British public gripped by "mania" as the medieval artwork depicting the Norman conquest of England goes on display outside France for the first time.

rfi.title: Podcast: Eco-anger, France in space, world's first photograph
rfi.description: A climate expert experiences eco-anxiety firsthand after living through France's hottest summer on record. France tries to find its place in the new space race. And the story of the earliest known photograph still visible today.

rfi.title: August hottest month ever recorded globally, says EU monitor
rfi.description: The EU's climate monitor said Thursday that August was the hottest single month ever recorded globally, with ocean temperatures also reaching unprecedented highs as western Europe capped its warmest summer.

rfi.title: Former PM Bayrou returns to court in long-running EU assistants case
rfi.description: Former French prime minister François Bayrou returns to court in Paris on Wednesday as an appeal opens into allegations that European Parliament funds were misused to pay staff working for his centrist MoDem party.

rfi.description: Ferran Torres hit a hat trick and Ousmane Dembélé scored twice on Wednesday night as Paris Saint-Germain crushed Slovan Bratislava 6-1 to launch the defence of their Champions League title.

lemonde.description: Le ministre de l’action et des comptes publics, David Amiel, a déclaré, vendredi, que les modalités de la mesure seraient arbitrées « prochainement » par Matignon.

lemonde.description: Depuis le début de la guerre au Moyen-Orient, Riyad a accru le recours à cet oléoduc, qui relie Abqaïq, près du Golfe, au port de Yanbou, sur la mer Rouge, pour contourner le verrouillage du détroit d’Ormuz par l’Iran.

lemonde.description: L’agent d’Anthropic a traduit cette preuve d’une complexité hors norme dans un langage de programmation, permettant de la vérifier automatiquement. Cette expérience ouvre la voie à de possibles progrès dans la validation des résultats mathématiques.

lemonde.title: A l’affiche de « Notre salut », Swann Arlaud, un acteur de convictions
lemonde.description: A 45 ans, le comédien révélé par « Petit paysan » demeure fidèle à ses convictions fortement ancrées à gauche. En mai, il a signé la tribune « Zapper Bolloré », au risque de voir sa carrière fragilisée.  En attendant, Swann Arlaud joue un fonctionnaire happé par la collaboration dans le nouveau film d’Emmanuel Marre.

lemonde.title: Le XXIᵉ siècle a-t-il vraiment débuté avec le 11-Septembre ?
lemonde.description: Par leur caractère inédit, les attentats de New York, en 2001, ont immédiatement donné le sentiment d’entrer dans un autre monde. Pourtant, d’autres ruptures majeures peuvent prétendre au titre d’acte de naissance de notre époque.

lemonde.title: Prison ferme pour un parent d’élève : un « signal fort » face aux violences contre les enseignants
lemonde.description: Un père de famille a été condamné à six mois de prison ferme, jeudi, pour avoir menacé de « couper la tête » d’une enseignante de l’école de son fils au Fauga (Haute-Garonne). lemonde.description: Le leader de La France insoumise a été interrogé par la rédaction de « L’Humanité » lors du traditionnel rendez-vous de rentrée du PCF, au Plessis-Pâté (Essonne), après le débat entre Fabien Roussel et Patrick Martin.

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, la forte inflation grève le pouvoir d’achat des Américains
lemonde.description: L’indice des prix à la consommation a augmenté de 3,4 % sur un an en août, selon les chiffres officiels publiés vendredi. Une hausse portée par l’envolée des coûts des carburants, durement ressentie par les ménages, à deux mois des élections de mi-mandat.

lemonde.title: L’Ultimate Championship, la nouvelle compétition qui veut encore une fois révolutionner l’athlétisme
lemonde.description: La Fédération internationale d’athlétisme lance, vendredi à Budapest, un nouveau championnat pensé pour améliorer le spectacle et l’exposition de cet ensemble de disciplines sportives.

lemonde.description: « Les sanctions doivent être mises en œuvre maintenant », a déclaré le président ukrainien, évoquant le projet de loi américain qui, selon l’agence Bloomberg, doit être soumis la semaine prochaine à la Chambre des représentants américains.

lemonde.title: En Ukraine, dans le village martyr d’Andriïvka, antre du « boucher de Boutcha »
lemonde.description: Ce sont les hommes du colonel Azatbek Omourbekov, sacré « héros de la Russie », qui, en mars 2022, ont perpétré les massacres d’Ukrainiens dans la région de Kiev. « Le Monde » a retrouvé la trace de ce jeune colonel dans l’école d’un village ukrainien proche de la capitale, Andriïvka, d’où il donnait ses ordres.

lemonde.title: Au Brésil, l’accès à Internet fait entrer les peuples amazoniens dans la campagne présidentielle : « Cela montre aux politiques ce qui arrive ici ! »
lemonde.description: Grâce à des antennes Starlink installées par une alliance d’organisations locales, des milliers de villages isolés d’Amazonie accèdent pour la première fois à Internet – et à une information politique jusque-là hors de portée, avant le scrutin du 4 octobre.

lemonde.title: Le prêtre directeur de l’Institution des Chartreux de Lyon, mis en retrait par l’archevêché, visé par une plainte pour viols et agressions sexuelles
lemonde.description: Le parquet de Lyon, qui avait déjà ouvert une enquête après un signalement du diocèse, a confirmé vendredi le dépôt de cette plainte par une ancienne étudiante.

The family of a British father who was found dead in the Caribbean in January is urging authorities in Grenada to work with UK police to uncover the truth about his death.

france24fr.title: Victoire de l'AfD en Saxe-Anhalt, campagne en Israël, commémorations du 11-09 aux Etats-Unis
france24fr.description: Au sommaire cette semaine, la victoire historique de l' AfD en Saxe-Anhalt et l'onde de choc que cela a représenté en Europe; les révélations du journal Haaretz qui plombent la campagne de Benyamin Netanyahou pour les législatives en Israël; et Donald Trump qui tente de remobiliser son camp à l'approche des mid-terms avec une "convention" républicaine à Dallas centrée sur sa personne.

france24fr.title: Reed Brody: "la tragédie du 11 septembre 2001 a été aggravée par la réponse qui y a été apportée"
france24fr.description: Les Etats-Unis commémorent le 25ème anniversaire des attentats du 11 septembre 2001. L'occasion de revenir sur 25 ans de lutte anti-terroriste, qui s'est accompagnée de nombreuses dérives en matières de droits humains: torture, prisons secrètes, justice "alternative". L'avocat américain Reed Brody, ancien substitut du procureur de l'Etat de New-York, ancien conseiller de l'ONG Human Rights Watch, était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : l'Arabie saoudite ferme temporairement l'oléoduc Est-Ouest au lendemain d'attaques houthies
Guerre en Ukraine : Zelensky exhorte Trump à adopter des sanctions "sévères" contre la Russie
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky a appelé vendredi Donald Trump à adopter "dès maintenant" des sanctions "sévères" contre la Russie, notamment pour freiner sa capacité à produire des missiles, dans un contexte d'intensification des frappes. Il a dit prévoir de rencontrer son homologue américain fin septembre à New York.

france24fr.title: Côte d'Ivoire : l'opposition veut peser sur la nouvelle Commission électorale
france24fr.description: 🇨🇮 En Côte d’Ivoire, l’opposition se concerte pour peser dans la constitution du nouvel organe électoral après la dissolution de la CEI. Réunis à plusieurs reprises, ses partis préparent une proposition commune au gouvernement.

france24fr.title: En marge du procès à Paris de l'assassinat de Federico Aramburu, les hommages se multiplient
france24fr.description: Au cours de la première semaine d'auditions à la cour d'assises de Paris portant sur l'assassinat de Federico Aramburu, les deux hommes accusés d'avoir abattu en mars 2022 l'ancien rugbyman argentin ont donné leur version. Un procès à forte connotation politique qui suscite une grande émotion chez les proches de "Fede".

france24fr.title: Légendes urbaines avec Jewel Usain
france24fr.description: Rendez-vous avec le rappeur Jewel Usain. En quinze ans de carrière, le chanteur a su constamment se distinguer par la très grande qualité de ses œuvres. Ovni dans l’univers du rap, il réussit à conquérir, avec patience et endurance, un public chaque jour plus nombreux. Dans cet épisode, la star du rap Japonais Acchi Mello et son ami d’enfance Guillaume lui offrent les vidéos surprises.

france24fr.title: Madagascar : Michaël Randrianirina et Macron tente de reconstruire un partenariat solide
france24fr.description: Le président malgache Michaël Randrianirina a été reçu à Paris ce jeudi 10 septembre par Emmanuel macron, c'est la deuxième rencontre entre les deux chef d'État depuis le changement de régime à Madagascar. Les deux hommes tentent de reconstruire un partenariat solide alors que les rapprochements de Madagascar avec la Russie inquiètent l'Élysée. Explications d'Aurélie Kouman, correspondante France 24 à Madagascar.

france24fr.title: Commémoration du 11 septembre : Zohran Mamdani présent aux côtés des anciens présidents américains
france24fr.description: Pour la cérémonie de commémoration des attentats du 11 septembre 2001, Donald Trump ne sera pas présent à Ground Zero. Le vice-président JD Vance sera lui à New York aux côtés des quatre anciens chefs d'Etat américains encore en vie. En bonne place à leurs côtés figurera le premier maire de la ville à avoir prêté serment sur un Coran, Zohran Mamdani, 34 ans, issu de la gauche du Parti démocrate. Un décryptage d'Anne Corpet, chroniqueuse à France 24.

france24fr.title: Allemagne, rechute à l'extrême droite ?
france24fr.description: La très large victoire de l'AfD dans le Land de Saxe-Anhalt réveille de douloureux souvenirs en Allemagne et en Europe. Est-ce la fin d'un interdit moral ? Pour en parler, notre invitée : l'historienne Hélène Miard-Delacroix.

france24fr.title: France : la folie Céline Dion s'empare de Paris
france24fr.description: Depuis des semaines, Céline Dion est partout dans Paris. La chanteuse québécoise donnera son premier concert samedi soir dans la capitale. Sa venue, ainsi que celle du pape Léon XIV le week-end du 25 septembre, devrait avoir des retombées économiques situées entre 500 et 800 millions d'euros pour la France.

france24fr.title: Automobile : les constructeurs européens en difficulté pendant que la Chine s'exporte
france24fr.description: La voiture fait sa révolution. Depuis maintenant plusieurs années, l'émergence des véhicules électriques a fait entrer toute une industrie dans une nouvelle ère. Une transformation qui s'est accélérée depuis quelques mois : la guerre au Moyen-Orient a fait flamber les prix du pétrole et les utilisateurs de voitures thermiques payent la facture à la pompe. Aujourd'hui, malgré un surcoût, l'électrique se présente comme une solution.

france24fr.title: Tchad - Libye : une coopération fragile autour de l'or dans la région du Tibesti
france24fr.description: Le Tchad tente de sécuriser sa frontière nord, celle qu’il partage avec la Libye. Depuis plusieurs mois, N’Djaména renforce ses relations autant avec le gouvernement d’union nationale libyen qu'avec les forces du maréchal Khalifa Haftar. Dans la région du Tibesti, l’état et les groupes anciennement rebelles entretiennent une coopération fragile autour de l’extraction d’or.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : une restriction des réseaux sociaux pour les moins de 16 ans en Californie
france24fr.description: La Californie vient d'instaurer un premier cadre réglementaire afin de protéger les moins de 16 ans des réseaux sociaux et de l'intelligence artificielle. Le gouverneur Gavin Newsom assure que son dispositif est plus efficace que les mesures prises en Australie.

france24fr.title: 11-Septembre : Donald Trump assure que les victimes ne seront jamais oubliées
france24fr.description:
🇺🇸 Le président américain Donald Trump a commémoré vendredi le 25e anniversaire des attentats du 11 septembre lors d’une cérémonie au Pentagone en hommage aux victimes.
 
🗽Les attentats, perpétrés par des membres d’Al-Qaïda, avaient fait près de 3 000 morts sur trois sites aux États-Unis et profondément marqué la politique étrangère et la sécurité nationale du pays.

france24fr.title: En Malaisie, des discours anti-Rohingya aux conséquences réelles
france24fr.description: Contenus hostiles sur les réseaux sociaux, désinformation, pétition réclamant leur départ du pays… : en Malaisie, les réfugiés Rohingya - une minorité majoritairement musulmane chassée de Birmanie - sont victimes de discours de rejet, qui ont notamment entraîné l’expulsion  de plus de 100 personnes d'un village et la fermeture temporaire d’écoles accueillant des enfants réfugiés.

france24fr.title: Emma Bonino, grande figure féministe italienne, est morte à 78 ans
france24fr.description: L'Italienne Emma Bonino, figure du féminisme et l'une des personnalités politiques les plus populaires dans son pays, est morte à l'âge de 78 ans. L'Italienne a lutté pendant cinq décennies pour de nombreuses causes sociales comme le droit au divorce, celui à l'avortement, la législation de l'euthanasie ou l'abolition de la peine de mort. Axelle Simon, journaliste à France 24, revient sur son parcours en image.

france24fr.title: Attentats du 11 septembre : un devoir de transmission envers la jeunesse américaine
france24fr.description: Plus le temps passe, plus la question de la mémoire de la transmission est posée concernant les attentats du 11 septembre 2001. La jeunesse états-unienne n'a pas connu ces attaques no leur retentissement pourtant bien ancré dans la mémoire collective. Le devoirs de ceux qui étaient là est alors de transmette leur savoir et de continuer de rendre hommage aux 2 977 victimes, civils et pompiers

zeit.title: Basketball: Alba verliert Testspiel gegen Euroleague-Team knapp
Energie: Saudi-Arabien schaltet nach Angriffen wichtige Pipeline ab
Queerfeindlichkeit: AfD-Wahlsieg in Sachsen-Anhalt verstärkt Sorgen queerer Menschen
zeit.description: Der Wahlsieg der AfD verstärkt das feindselige Klima gegen queere Menschen. Laut dem Verband »Queere Vielfalt« werden Menschenrechte »aktiv bedroht«.

zeit.title: Fußball-Bundesliga: Leipzig-Chef nach nächster Pleite: «Wir bleiben ruhig»
2. Fußball-Bundesliga: «Spitzenreiter»: Nürnberg feiert nach der Energieleistung
Region Archangelsk: Zwölf Tote bei Autounfall in Russland
2. Fußball-Bundesliga: Titz unter Druck: Hannover 96 verliert auch in Nürnberg
Fußball-Regionalliga: Überragender Fiedler: 1860 München holt ersten Heimsieg
9/11 Terroranschlag: Als ein Land sich selbst verlor
zeit.description: Einwanderung als Frage nationaler Sicherheit, Migranten als Gefahr, gegen die jedes Mittel recht ist – Donald Trumps Grausamkeit ist ohne den 11. September kaum denkbar.

zeit.title: Anschlag auf das World Trade Center: Der Mann in der Wolke
zeit.description: Sein Vater Sebastian Gorki starb beim Anschlag auf das World Trade Center, ein halbes Jahr vor Nicholas’ Geburt. Wie lebt es sich mit diesem Erbe?

zeit.title: 3. Fußball-Liga: 0:4 in Köln: Erste Niederlage für Hansa in Drittliga-Saison
Abkommen mit Drittstaaten: Für manche Partner ist schon das Wort »Rückkehr« ein Problem
zeit.description: Europa will Menschen in Staaten außerhalb der EU überstellen. Wie schwer Vereinbarungen mit Drittstaaten sind, hat unser Autor in Verhandlungen für Frontex erlebt.

zeit.title: CDU: Christina Stumpp legt Amt als Vize-Generalsekretärin der CDU nieder
zeit.description: Die stellvertretende CDU-Generalsekretärin Stumpp scheidet aus dem Amt. Zuvor hatte sie entsprechende Berichte dementiert. Ein Nachfolger steht offenbar bereits fest.

zeit.title: Dokumentarfilm »Naza«: Israels Armee bestreitet KI-gesteuerte Tötungen im Gazastreifen
zeit.description: Israels Militär hat den im Dokumentarfilm »Naza« erhobenen Vorwürfen widersprochen. Über Angriffe im Gazastreifen hätten immer Menschen entschieden, nicht Maschinen.

zeit.title: Erfolg der AfD: Wie die AfD Liebe zur Strategie macht
zeit.description: Warum nur ist die AfD so erfolgreich? Weil sie es geschafft hat, das schönste Gefühl der Welt für sich zu instrumentalisieren – etwa in der Familienpolitik.

nzz.title: Ultimate Championship: Werro siegt im Halbfinal
nzz.description: Audrey Werro zeigt sich auch bei der Premiere der Ultimate Championships in Budapest in toller Form. Die Europameisterin über 800 m qualifiziert sich souverän für den Final vom Samstag.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Namen, Blumen, Stille: So gedenkt New York der Opfer von 9/11
nzz.description: 2977 Leben wurden am 11. September 2001 ausgelöscht. Ein Vierteljahrhundert später erinnert Amerika an die Opfer einer Tragödie, die die Welt für immer veränderte.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Russen sollen zwei ukrainische Gefangene erschossen haben +++ Modi drängt Putin erneut zu Friedensverhandlungen
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Kultur: Céline Dion will nach Krankheitspause Bühnen-Comeback feiern
Ständemehr für die EU-Verträge: Ehemaliger Bundesrichter kritisiert den Bundesrat
nzz.description: Für Hansjörg Seiler ist klar: Der Bundesrat interpretiert die Verfassung falsch, weshalb das Parlament ihn nun korrigieren soll.

nzz.title: Nach dem Brand der Fähre auf den Philippinen: 35 Tote geborgen
nzz.description: Auf einer Fähre, die zwischen philippinischen Inseln unterwegs war, ist am Mittwoch ein Feuer ausgebrochen. Mindestens 35 Menschen sind tot. Viele Passagiere werden noch vermisst.

nzz.title: Könnte KI uns alle umbringen? Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten zur Debatte um die KI-Apokalypse
nzz.description: Ein Angestellter verlässt das KI-Startup Anthropic und warnt davor, künstliche Intelligenz könnte die Menschheit ausrotten. Was hinter solchen Aussagen steckt und warum sie gerade häufiger werden.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: In Niger entführte Schweizerin offenbar freigelassen +++ Bundesrat will Zivilstand «geschieden» abschaffen
Ein kleiner Verlag will den «ultimativen Skandal» inszenieren – und entlarvt damit den Schweizer Literaturbetrieb und sich selbst
nzz.description: Der Th.-Gut-Verlag verkauft Geschichten. Mal zwischen Buchdeckeln, mal aus der Trickkiste. Denn am Ende gilt: Es gibt keine schlechte Presse. Eine kleine Posse.

nzz.title: Wer im Schweizer Triathlon Erfolg haben will, trainiert bei Brett Sutton – und bekommt Unterstützung aus China
nzz.description: Die Langdistanz-Triathletinnen Julie Derron und Alanis Siffert zählen an der Ironman-70.3-WM in Nizza zu den Favoritinnen.

nzz.title: Kurz nach ihrem Bruder König Harald: Prinzessin Astrid ist tot
nzz.description: Erst vor zwei Wochen starb ihr Bruder König Harald V. Nun ist auch Haralds ältere Schwester Prinzessin Astrid tot. Die 94-Jährige starb nur zwei Tage nach dem Staatsbegräbnis des Monarchen.

nzz.title: Der frühere SFV-Präsident Ralph Zloczower ist gestorben. Er führte den Verband acht Jahre lang
nzz.description: Zloczower wurde 93 Jahre alt. In seine Zeit als Verbandspräsident fällt die Euro 2008 – als erstmals seit 50 Jahren wieder ein Sportanlass in dieser Grössenordnung in der Schweiz stattfand.

nzz.title: Münchner Wirt scheitert vorläufig mit Klage gegen Bierzelt-Vergabe am Oktoberfest
nzz.description: Wer darf am Oktoberfest ein Bierzelt aufstellen? Ein Wirt prangert die tradierte Ordnung auf der Wiesn an. Eine Woche vor dem Fest landet der Streit vor Gericht.

nzz.title: Ein prominenter früherer Gefangener aus Weissrussland wagt die Heimreise und testet damit Lukaschenko
nzz.description: Der auf Druck der USA freigelassene Dissident Andrzej Poczobut besucht in der Heimat die unterdrückte polnische Minderheit. Das weissrussische Regime will sich wieder dem Westen annähern. Die Vereinigten Staaten versuchen das auszunutzen.

nzz.title: «Ich schneide dir den Kopf ab!» – ein Vater bedroht die Lehrerin seines Sohnes und wird zu sechs Monaten Haft verurteilt
nzz.description: Der Fall ist symptomatisch für die Gewalt, der französische Lehrer ausgesetzt sind. Und er weckt Erinnerungen an den Mord an Samuel Paty.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Krise bei Volkswagen: VW-Tochter Porsche verkauft Beteiligungen an Bugatti Rimac und Rimac Group +++ Arbeitnehmer wollen VW-Vorstand zu Gesprächen zwingen
nzz.description: Der Volkswagen-Konzern steht vor einem einschneidenden Umbau. Bis 2030 wird Europas grösster Autobauer 50 000 weitere Stellen abbauen. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

observador.title: Criação. DGArtes apoia 84 projetos e deixa 158 de fora
observador.description: Concurso de Programação do Programa de Apoio a Projetos 2025 contou com 275 candidaturas, 189 das quais ficaram sem apoio. A larga maioria, 158, não receberá qualquer verba.

observador.title: Municípios do Oeste pedem declaração desfavorável para mina
observador.description: Conselho da OesteCIM manifestou "posição desfavorável" ao projeto por considerá-lo "incompatível com a capacidade de suporte ambiental e territorial da área envolvente".

observador.title: Britânico usava fórum online para incentivar crimes sexuais
observador.description: Darren Conway terá solicitado imagens de mulheres nuas enquanto dormiam ou estavam inconscientes em pelo menos 10 ocasiões. Leitura de sentença marcada para 30 de outubro.

observador.title: OE. Câmara de Gaia quer eliminação de pórticos na A29 e A32
observador.description: Proposta tornada pública pelo presidente Luís Filipe Menezes de incluir a eliminação do pórtico na A29 no Orçamento foi aprovada em reunião privada. A essa proposta soma-se o pórtico na A32.

observador.title: Governo investe 500 milhões de euros em 402 centros
observador.description: Segundo o ministro da Educação, o investimento integrado foi além da meta definida, resultando na criação de mais 40 centros tecnológicos especializados do que estava inicialmente previsto.

observador.title: Cabo Verde recebeu mais 9% de hóspedes no segundo trimestre
observador.description: Cabo Verde recebeu mais 9% em comparação com 2025. Contabilizando 277 mil hóspedes no segundo trimestre. Um quarto dos quais oriundo do Reino Unido, principal país de origem.

observador.title: As notícias das 20h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: PSP deteve adepto interditado no Estádio do Dragão
observador.description: O adepto detido está impedido de entrar em recintos desportivos desde novembro de 2025. A sanção foi-lhe aplicada devido ao incumprimento dos deveres de moderação e respeito durante um jogo.

observador.title: GNR deteve 173 suspeitos do crime de incêndio em 2026
observador.description: "Dos últimos 10 anos, é claramente o ano com maior número de detenções" afirmou o diretor do SEPNA. Em 2025, a GNR deteve 68 suspeitos do crime de incêndio florestal.

observador.title: Viseu alarga perímetro de equipas de apoio à saúde mental
observador.description: Equipa intervém atualmente em Vouzela, Oliveira de Frades, São Pedro do Sul e Castro Daire. Expansão prevê alargar atividade ao concelhos de Vila Nova de Paiva, Sátão e Aguiar da Beira.

observador.title: JPP requer inquérito parlamentar sobre atuação de Luís Neves
observador.description: Pedido de inquérito não tem caráter potestativo e só se concretizará se for aprovado em plenário. Chega também entregou requerimento, mas ainda não foi admitido.

observador.title: APG/GNR: “Não desconvocamos sem propostas concretas”
observador.description: O Presidente da estrutura, César Nogueira, sinaliza, ainda assim, disponibilidade para negociar com o Governo. Os militares da GNR querem que a revisão dos salários e das carreiras entre no OE2027.

observador.title: Putin acusa Ocidente de recorrer a "formas pouco dignas"
observador.description: Vladimir Putin diz também que foram impostas mais de 30 mil sanções à Rússia, mas garante que são os países europeus que estão a sofrer com as penalizações a Moscovo.

observador.title: UE aprova verba de 6,1 mil milhões para apoio à Ucrânia
observador.description: A parcela de 6,1 mil milhões de euros faz parte do empréstimo de 90 mil milhões de euros aprovado pelos 27 para apoiar a Ucrânia neste e no próximo ano.

observador.title: O plano de Passos Coelho para o País
observador.description: Passos vai apresentar propostas reformistas dentro de dois meses. Enquanto não são públicas, dá pistas sobre o plano que tem para o País num longo prefácio do novo livro de Pedro Gomes Sanches.

observador.title: DECO questiona legalidade da tarifa fixa dos táxis em Lisboa
observador.description: Associação Portuguesa para a Defesa do Consumidor questiona legalidade do protocolo assinado esta sexta-feira, que prevê preços fixos de 16 ou 19 euros para deslocações diurnas em dias úteis.

observador.title: Pais processam Ministério da Educação por falta de vagas
observador.description: Pais enviaram emails, fizeram telefonemas e endereçaram queixas junto dos serviços do ministério. Mas nunca obtiveram resposta. "Não há forma de contacto presencial", dizem.

observador.title: CGTP quer aumento do salário mínimo para 1.100 euros em 2027
observador.description: Central sindical apresenta uma proposta salarial que defende aumentos de pelo menos 15%. "Trabalhadores precisam de salários que permitam viver dignamente durante todo o ano e não num só período."

spiegel.title: Diktatorenvergleiche – Mbappé beklagt »mangelndes politisches Bewusstsein«
spiegel.description: Fußballstar Kylian Mbappé gilt auf und neben dem Platz als dominante Person. Social-Media-Memes zeigen den Stürmer deshalb als Diktator. Mbappé hat nun deutlich gemacht: Deren Urheber hält er für dumm.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: Ölteppich breitet sich nach US-Angriff in der Straße von Hormus aus
spiegel.description: Satellitenbilder zeigen Ölschlieren nahe der umkämpften Meerenge. Die Verschmutzung könnte von einem beladenen Tanker stammen, den die USA am Dienstag versenkt haben.

spiegel.title: Nadelöhr Bab al-Mandab: Droht im Nahen Osten die nächste Seeblockade?
spiegel.description: Der Bürgerkrieg im Jemen eskaliert, die Huthi-Miliz rückt auf strategisch entscheidende Orte vor. Das könnte dramatische Auswirkungen auf den Welthandel haben.

spiegel.title: Ebola im Kongo: Neuer Todesfall im Nordwesten verschärft die Lage
spiegel.description: Ein neuer Ebola-Toter außerhalb des bisherigen Ausbruchsgebiets verschärft die Lage in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo. Die Behörden rechnen mit zahlreichen Kontaktpersonen und verstärken die Suche nach weiteren Infizierten.

spiegel.title: CDU: Stellvertretende Generalsekretärin Christina Stumpp tritt nun doch ab
spiegel.description: Der Kanzler will die CDU-Zentrale neu aufstellen – eigentlich. Aber Vizegeneralsekretärin Christina Stumpp hat ihre Entlassung lange verweigert. Jetzt hat Friedrich Merz sich doch noch durchgesetzt.

spiegel.title: Christian von Stetten: Für den CDU-Politiker ist Bärbel Bas als Ministerin »nicht mehr tragbar«
spiegel.description: Der einflussreiche CDU-Abgeordnete Christian von Stetten übt in der »Bild« deutliche Kritik an der Arbeitsministerin und teilt auch gegen Finanzminister Klingbeil aus. Die Reaktionen aus der SPD sind scharf.

spiegel.title: 9/11 im historischen Liveticker: Feuerwehrleute retten überlebende Kameraden und Zivilisten aus Trümmern
spiegel.description: Einsatzkräfte bergen Menschen aus den Trümmern des World Trade Center. Hunderte Tote werden befürchtet. US-Präsident Bush richtet sich an die Bevölkerung. Dieser Liveblog rekonstruiert den Terroranschlag vom 11. September 2001.

spiegel.title: Filmfestival in Venedig: Russell Crowe präsentiert Musik-Doku »What Love Builds«
spiegel.description: Der »Gladiator«-Star präsentiert in Venedig seinen Musikdokumentarfilm »What Love Builds«. Dabei spricht er über seine Karriere, kommende Projekte und den Wunsch, mehr Zeit mit seinen Söhnen zu verbringen.

spiegel.title: USA: Wie Donald Trump eine Blamage der Republikaner bei den Midterms abwenden will
spiegel.description: Den Republikanern droht bei den Kongresswahlen im November eine Schlappe. Bei dem Sonderparteitag in Dallas wird deutlich, auf welche Strategie die GOP setzt – und dass manche darin ein Risiko sehen.

spiegel.title: »Zauberhafte Schwestern 2« mit Sandra Bullock & Nicole Kidman: Der erstaunlich altmodische Zaubertrick dieser Fortsetzung
spiegel.description: Sandra Bullock und Nicole Kidman kehren in »Zauberhafte Schwestern 2« als Hexenschwestern zurück. Die Fortsetzung beschwört zwar weibliche Solidarität, führt ihre Heldinnen aber oft über Männer zurück zur eigenen Macht.

spiegel.title: Beringmeer vor Alaska: 15-Jähriger überlebt tagelang auf gekentertem Boot
spiegel.description: Ohne Wasser und Essen ist ein Teenager mehrere Tage auf einem gekenterten Boot über die Beringsee getrieben, bis er gerettet wurde. Sein älterer Bruder und sein Cousin kamen ums Leben.

spiegel.title: Nepal: Warum das Land nach der Sturzflut im Himalaya Entschädigungen fordert
spiegel.description: Nepal fordert nach der Flutkatastrophe Entschädigungen von Ländern mit hohem CO₂-Ausstoß. Bisher verweigern die solche Zahlungen, doch die Idee könnte eine neue Chance bekommen.

spiegel.title: Sterbehilfe: Britisches Parlament lehnt Legalisierung in erster Lesung ab
spiegel.description: Ein Gesetzentwurf zur Legalisierung der Sterbehilfe in England und Wales ist unerwartet vorerst vom Tisch. Auch in Deutschland wird seit Jahren über Regelungen zum assistierten Suizid diskutiert.

spiegel.title: Landtagswahl in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Diese Regierungen sind möglich
spiegel.description: Neue Umfragen zeigen, wie eng das Rennen um Platz eins ist – und wie schwierig die Regierungsbildung in Schwerin werden könnte. Testen Sie mit unserem Rechner, wann welche Konstellation möglich wird.

spiegel.title: Österreich: Ehefrau starb nach mutmaßlichem Missbrauch durch Ehemann

phys-org.title: Bite, buzz, release: How bees make flowers give up their pollen
phys-org.description: Life is not always easy for a bee: Not all plants place their pollen outside. Some flowers have to be set to vibrating before the pollen can get out of their tube-like stamens. Certain bee species have developed a special technique for this: They bite on the flower and use their flight muscles to generate rapid vibrations. The stamen is shaken and the pollen is released. This phenomenon is known as "buzz pollination."

phys-org.title: Unusual bonds reorganize structure and magnetism in vanadium material
phys-org.description: While chemical bonds usually determine the structure and properties of a material, bonds between neighboring metal atoms can also change as temperature or other conditions change. These changes can lead to unusual electronic and magnetic behaviors.

phys-org.title: Shapeshifting plant roots rely on a balance of anatomy, metabolism, and microbes to maximize survival
phys-org.description: Scientists have identified the mechanisms that allow plants to change their root anatomy to maximize survival when nutrients are scarce. The findings could pave the way for developing new ways to improve beneficial plant-microbe interactions in agriculture.

phys-org.title: Scientists discover a strange new form of ice that could help explain the interiors of Neptune and Uranus
phys-org.description: Scientists have discovered that there is ice deep inside planets like Neptune and Uranus and want to find out what form it takes and how it behaves. They cannot dig for it and transport it all the way back to Earth, so they do the next best thing: recreate those extreme conditions in the lab.

phys-org.title: Smart pen detects pressure and movement to identify children's writing difficulties sooner
phys-org.description: A study by Politecnico di Milano and the University of Insubria (Varese and Como) has been published in PLOS Digital Health. The study involved more than 700 children from primary and lower secondary school. The participants used the THInkPen (Tele-Health Ink Pen) while completing two BVSCO-3 tasks from the Battery for the Clinical Assessment of Writing and Orthographic Skills. This is the most widely used test in Italy for assessing writing difficulties, dysgraphia and dysorthography.

phys-org.title: Fertilizers and extreme heat are damaging coral reefs in the Gulf of Mexico, isotope analyses reveal
phys-org.description: Who isn't familiar with the colorful coral reefs from movies like "Finding Nemo" or "The Little Mermaid"? Unfortunately, the reality is often quite different, as these vital ecosystems are under pressure worldwide. Climate change and pollution are causing corals to bleach and die. Even the most resilient coral reefs of the United States are now threatened.

phys-org.title: Giant volcanic blanket reveals hidden 'Pompeii' of Andean landscapes
phys-org.description: A vast sheet of volcanic rock in the Andes has preserved clues to a buried landscape that existed 22 million years ago, according to a new study led by UCL (University College London) researchers.

phys-org.title: New study offers a detailed look at how wildfire smoke impacts Reno's air quality
phys-org.description: With Western wildfires increasing in size, duration and intensity, millions of Americans are now exposed to wildfire smoke each year. In California, 2020 and 2021 were particularly challenging, with a 10-fold increase in fires compared with any time in the state's history. phys-org.title: AI extracts interpretable constitutive laws directly from solid-mechanics data
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Eastern Institute of Technology (EIT), Ningbo, have developed a graph-based approach that directly extracts concise, accurate constitutive equations from solid-material experimental data. The study, published in Science Advances, describes a method for discovering constitutive models for alloy steels, lithium metal and filled rubbers. It outperforms mainstream empirical models in predictive accuracy while preserving explicit, physically interpretable mathematical formulations.

phys-org.title: Healthy checkout policy shows promise for reducing soda sales and increasing healthy snack purchases
phys-org.description: In March 2021, Berkeley, Calif., became the first city in the world to ban the display of sugary beverages and snacks in store checkout lanes, where candy, chocolate and soda are commonly placed to encourage impulse buying while shoppers are in line.

phys-org.title: Project RattleCam reveals baby snakes during birthing season in three US states for the first time
phys-org.description: It's the season for babies in the snake world, and Project RattleCam is capturing magical moments.

phys-org.title: Brain's ability to hear a musical beat remains distinctly human, study suggests
phys-org.description: The seemingly trivial ability to hear a regular pulse in music is a remarkable—and perhaps distinctively human—feature of the brain. In a wide-ranging critical review, Gábor Háden of the HUN-REN Research Centre for Natural Sciences and Henkjan Honing of the University of Amsterdam evaluate more than two decades of research into how this capacity develops and has evolved. Their paper was published this week in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences.

phys-org.title: Travel bots are making decisions for us—convenient, but should we trust them?
phys-org.description: Imagine telling your phone that you want a quiet boutique hotel near a city center, below a certain price, with a decent breakfast and late checkout. A few seconds later, an AI assistant compares the options, explains why each one fits and helps complete the booking. This is no longer hypothetical.

phys-org.title: Electrical pulses convert PFAS waste into valuable silver fluoride
phys-org.description: Fluorinated waste, like that found in firefighting aqueous film-forming foam, can act as a significant environmental pollutant. Recently, James Tour's lab at Rice University developed a method to capture fluoride from these waste streams and recycle it into a useful reagent, silver fluoride, that could be used in other manufacturing processes. This process is published in Nature Chemical Engineering.

phys-org.title: Why making friends at university feels harder than it really is
phys-org.description: The summer before starting university can bring multiple worries for students: worrying about obtaining a place in a desired program, navigating the clearing process to confirm a place, securing housing, sorting out financial aid, preparing for academic study and even finding the right school supplies.

phys-org.title: Libraries are a lifeline, new research finds
phys-org.description: New research has highlighted the important role public libraries play in supporting communities, helping people build connections, access support and improve their well-being through everyday interactions.

phys-org.description: For the first time, important features of the Antarctic coastal zone have been mapped at high resolution around the continent by training an artificial intelligence tool to accurately recognize grounded icebergs in satellite radar images.

undark.title: Review: A Vision of a Future Where Machines Fight Wars
undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

proj-syn.title: AI Could Make Governments Slower
proj-syn.description: Governments are increasingly turning to AI tools to process vast amounts of information and make public services more efficient. But because human attention is finite, making machines more capable could simply create new bottlenecks wherever oversight is necessary.

proj-syn.title: Why Do So Few Women Work in India?
proj-syn.description: India’s female labor force participation rate has long lagged behind that of peer economies like Bangladesh, not because of social norms, but because of weak demand for labor. That is ultimately good news, because it is a problem that can be solved with common-sense regulatory reforms and public investment.

proj-syn.title: Global Development’s Missing Ingredient
proj-syn.description: Facing a democracy deficit worldwide, millions of vulnerable people lack avenues through which they can collectively negotiate their interests. Faith-based institutions committed to human dignity and pluralism can play an instrumental role in building the infrastructure required for grassroots organizing at scale.

proj-syn.title: China’s External Surplus Makes a “Mandarin Accord” Inevitable
proj-syn.description: As with the Plaza Accord in 1985, when the United States and its major trading partners agreed to coordinate policies to weaken the US dollar, an agreement to address global imbalances emanating from China has become increasingly necessary. Given China’s undervalued currency, the situation simply cannot be sustained indefinitely.

proj-syn.title: War and Climate
proj-syn.description: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz showed how quickly a regional conflict can throw global energy markets into chaos. By pushing governments toward coal and biofuels, the war could accelerate deforestation and undermine climate negotiations, with environmental consequences that will linger long after the fighting ends.

proj-syn.title: 9/11’s Long Shadow
proj-syn.description: As tragic as the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, were, it was America’s response that truly changed the world. While it is difficult to pinpoint precisely which developments over the last 25 years were caused or compounded by 9/11, it seems clear that the event led the United States to abandon the principles that, with the Cold War over, were supposed to shape a better future.

proj-syn.title: The False Politics of Western Declinism
proj-syn.description: Political leaders on both sides of the Atlantic increasingly portray the West as being in decline, even as their societies grow richer. By conflating a loss of relative economic power with falling living standards, they give populists an opening to turn domestic grievances into nationalist resentment.

proj-syn.title: What 9/11 Did to Us
proj-syn.description: For Americans who are old enough to remember them, the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks raised fundamental questions: Who could have done this, and above all, why? We now know that the answers would reshape the country and its place in the world—and not for the better.

proj-syn.title: After the AI Bubble Bursts
proj-syn.description: Just as debt markets fueled the global financial near-meltdown that followed the 2007–08 subprime-mortgage crisis, their exposure to AI will drive developments now. The problem is that we possess only very limited public information about those markets, and regulators are not making that information any easier to obtain.

proj-syn.title: Trump Is Stoking Territorial Revisionism
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump’s refusal to respect international borders has already led Argentina and Morocco to revive territorial disputes and has effectively given Israel carte blanche to operate where it sees fit. But this might be just the beginning: if the US can claim land and resources on the basis of vague national-security claims, anyone can.

proj-syn.title: Have the Terrorists Won?
proj-syn.description: The point of terrorism is not to cause suffering, but to provoke the target into doing something that hurts it even more. In the quarter-century since the 9/11 attacks, the US has done just that, leaving the world and itself worse off.

proj-syn.title: How 9/11 Fractured the Global Order
proj-syn.description: The terrorist attack on the United States 25 years ago remains among the most consequential events of this century. By fundamentally altering the trajectories of the United States and Russia, as well as that of a rising China, al-Qaeda’s attack set in motion developments that would produce the geopolitical tumult we live in today.

proj-syn.title: China’s Permanent Manufacturing Revolution
proj-syn.description: In developed economies, manufacturing employment will decline, regardless of industrial strategies pursued. China's competitiveness means that any expectation that manufacturing will absorb more than a trivial fraction of the large increases in the working-age population still occurring in India or Africa is a delusion.

proj-syn.title: Europe Needs Dual-Use Defense Spending
proj-syn.description: Some EU countries, such as Poland, are using their expanded defense budgets to buy more foreign hardware. A better approach would be to foster a thriving innovation ecosystem which ensures that the technologies, institutions, and people that underpin a strong military benefit the civilian economy as well.

proj-syn.title: The World 9/11 Didn’t Make
proj-syn.description: Looking back at the past quarter-century, it becomes apparent that the 9/11 terrorist attack against the United States was not a transformative event. Far more important developments have intervened, not least America’s rejection of the postwar order that it had a large hand in building.

proj-syn.title: The BRICS at 20
proj-syn.description: If the promise of the BRICS was to establish a monetary union, a single market, or a tightly integrated political alliance, it has not been fulfilled. But if it was to build a platform for emerging economies to cooperate while advancing their own strategic autonomy, the BRICS has exceeded expectations.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Security Depends on a Clear Electrification Target
proj-syn.description: The politics around electrification are beginning to shift in Europe as more people recognize its importance for economic competitiveness and industrial resilience. European Union policymakers should seize this momentum to embed a binding target of at least 50% electrification by 2040 in the bloc’s energy security framework.
